title: Mounts
tagline: Every mount in Pywel you can keep — where it lives, how to make it yours, and what it is worth riding for.
asOf: Current to Charting the Unknown · November 2026

metrics.label: Speed
metrics.blurb: Top-end movement: the in-game Speed and Acceleration ratings for horses at max level, source descriptions for everything else.

metrics.label: Stamina
metrics.blurb: How long it can sprint, swim or fly before it slows: the in-game Stamina stat, or the use timer for timed mounts.

metrics.label: Travel
metrics.blurb: Total capacity to cover ground. Weighted mostly on speed, then stamina, then terrain traits — no fall damage, jumping, water sprint, flight — minus cooldown limits.

metrics.label: Combat
metrics.blurb: Mounted fighting value: Attack and Health, special attacks, and whether it keeps fighting after you dismount.

rules.text: A mount is ranked against others of its own class — Land, Sea (below the surface), Sky or Surface (ships) — so a Tier I sea mount is the best thing that swims, not the best mount overall.
A mount with a decisive trait scores higher on the metric that trait serves: no fall damage lifts Travel, a unique attack lifts Combat.
They grow with riding and trust; beasts and machines arrive at full strength.
marks a metric that does not apply, such as Stamina on a balloon, mech, wagon or ship.
Ratings are editorial calls built on recorded stats and the cited guides. Where no source compares a mount, it sits at Tier III and says so.

ladderNote: Tiers rank each mount against others of the same terrain. Ratings are editorial calls built on recorded stats and the cited guides.

leaves.label: Legendary
leaves.blurb: One of a kind: the three legendary horses, the sigil beasts, Blackstar, the legends of the deep and the four legendary ships.
leaves.short: One of a kind — each exists once in Pywel.

leaves.label: Rare
leaves.blurb: Never sold at a stable — stolen, subdued, hatched or raised, then taken in for good.
leaves.short: Never sold at a stable — stolen, subdued, hatched or raised.

leaves.label: Stable
leaves.blurb: The horse breeds you can tame, steal or buy, plus the soldiers' and scouts' horses you take off the road. They level up and learn skills as you ride.
leaves.short: Horses you tame, steal or buy, then register at a stable.

leaves.label: Engineered
leaves.blurb: Built or bought, not tamed: three balloons, two mechs, three wagons and the ships, made through your Greymane camp or bought from ship managers.
leaves.short: Built or bought — workshops, shipyards and ship managers.

lenses.label: All Around Best
lenses.blurb: The land mounts that do everything well, ranked on all four ratings together.

lenses.label: Battle
lenses.blurb: The strongest mounts to fight from, on land, at sea and in the air.

lenses.label: Cliffs & drops
lenses.blurb: Jumpers, climbers and gliders that turn cliffs into shortcuts.

lenses.label: Cargo
lenses.blurb: Extra carrying capacity for trading runs.

categories.label: Land
categories.blurb: Hooves, paws, claws and wheels — everything that covers ground.

categories.label: Underwater
categories.blurb: Below the surface: the 19 sea mounts of Charting the Unknown, plus the refitted A.T.A.G.

categories.label: Flying
categories.blurb: Every way into the sky: the dragon, the wyvern and three balloons.

categories.label: Ships
categories.blurb: Every hull you can own: the quest-built Greymane ships, the regional ships and rowboats at the Ship Managers, and the four legendary ships you build from blueprints.

categories.label: Mechanical
categories.blurb: Machines you pilot rather than ride: the A.T.A.G. and High-Mobility A.T.A.G. mechs and the three balloons.

categories.label: Easter Eggs
categories.blurb: Mounts that wink at other games, and rides the game never tells you about.

leaves.label: Oddities
leaves.short: Strange rides hidden in plain sight.
